chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife while he was absent; when does she observe the waiting period? He said: 'If evidence is established for her that she was divorced on a known day and a known month, let her observe the waiting period from the day she was divorced. And if she does not remember which day and which month, let her observe the waiting period from the day it reaches her.'
ai.seo_question: When does the waiting period begin for a woman whose husband divorced her while he was away?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural mechanics of the 'iddah' period when the husband is absent, emphasizing the evidentiary standard required to fix the start date. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that certainty (yaqin) regarding the divorce date anchors the waiting period, while uncertainty defaults to the date of notification, ensuring fairness in the woman's legal status. This distinction highlights the practical application of proof in family law, balancing textual certainty with the reality of delayed communication in pre-modern contexts.
